big_case.notes: Overton sought to halt his imminent execution. His challenge to Florida’s clemency process and access to its records could also affect other prisoners under warrant. The Court resolved this application and the linked petition in a brief order that announced no rule for future cases.

leakage.notes: Forward forecast made November 15. The historical corpus query and the captured Woodard lookup concern other cases. The two unobserved web calls target Woodard or its concurrence and can be assessed only from their queries. The rationale describes an application still pending on the opening docket. No query, result date or cited fact points to Overton’s November 19 disposition.

central_claims.basis: The complete disposing entry consists of two sentences. It names no author or dissenter, gives no reasons and records no separate writing. The first sentence denies the stay.
central_claims.claim: The Court will deny the stay in an unsigned order without a substantive majority opinion or a separate writing.

central_claims.basis: Florida filed its response on November 17. The docket shows no call for it and the outcome explicitly records response_requested as false.
central_claims.claim: The Circuit Justice will likely call for a response.

central_claims.basis: The November 19 order says the application was presented to Justice Thomas, referred by him to the Court, and denied. Its next sentence denies certiorari.
central_claims.claim: The Circuit Justice will refer the application to the full Court.

central_claims.basis: The November 19 docket lists only the application, Florida’s response, Overton’s reply, the referral and the order. The outcome records zero amicus briefs.
central_claims.claim: The amicus count will most likely stay at zero.

central_claims.basis: The docket confirms November 19, within the forecast window. It records no hour of issuance.
central_claims.claim: The Court will dispose of the stay November 16–19, before the scheduled 6 p.m. execution.
